procedure.description: infliximab injection, 10 mg units, induction for moderate to severe Crohn disease

denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for HCPCS J1745 (infliximab injection, 10 mg units, induction for moderate to severe Crohn disease) with date of service 2026-04-08. CARC 197: Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent. Payer remark: No authorization is on file. Under the plan terms, services rendered without prior authorization are not eligible for retrospective review. This is an administrative determination and not a medical necessity determination.

criteria.text: Moderately to severely active Crohn disease documented by a Harvey-Bradshaw Index of 8 or more (or Crohn Disease Activity Index of 220 or more), or endoscopic evidence of active disease.

Inadequate response, intolerance, or contraindication to conventional therapy with a corticosteroid course and an immunomodulator (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, or methotrexate), unless the disease is fistulizing.
Negative tuberculosis and hepatitis B screening before the first dose.
Prescribed by or in consultation with a gastroenterologist, at weight-based dosing of 5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6 for induction.

chart.text: Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.4, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 18 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
A1c came back 5.8. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Colonoscopy with ileal intubation. Deep serpiginous ulcers with cobblestoning in the terminal ileum and ascending colon, normal rectum and left colon. Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn Disease 14. Biopsies taken.
Vitamin D came back 20. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Terminal ileum and ascending colon biopsies: chronic active ileocolitis with crypt distortion and a non-necrotizing granuloma. Consistent with Crohn disease.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

30 year old man in gastroenterology follow-up for ileocolonic Crohn disease diagnosed 2 years ago. Missing work, up at night. Discussed moving to an anti-TNF agent, the infusion schedule, infection risk, and screening before the first dose. His history otherwise: migraines, rare now. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works in a warehouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Harvey-Bradshaw Index 13 today: 8 liquid stools a day, abdominal pain most days, feels generally unwell, down 14 pounds in 3 months.

Prednisone 40 daily with a taper starting 7 months ago, flared at 10 milligrams; second taper 4 months ago, flared again at 15. Azathioprine 150 daily (2.5 per kilo) for 5 months with therapeutic metabolite levels and no improvement in the Harvey-Bradshaw Index. Mesalamine stopped as ineffective.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Interferon-gamma release assay negative. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative, core antibody negative, surface antibody positive from vaccination. Chest X-ray clear. Hepatitis C antibody negative.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Screening labs reviewed and negative. Consent for infliximab signed. First infusion scheduled next week; the prior authorization request went in today. Vitals today 131 over 74, pulse 72.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Infliximab induction dose 1, 400 milligrams (5 per kilo at 88 kilograms) intravenous over 2 hours per gastroenterology, premedicated, tolerated without reaction. Week 2 and week 6 doses scheduled.

expected.note: CARC 197 is an administrative denial the chart cannot answer: the plan refuses retrospective review, so the remedy is a dispute of the authorization process, not a medical necessity appeal.
